findings.problem: The root finder of the notebooks is attributed to the Revision Rust solver. Line 1694 says the solver 'keeps an interval ... and halves it 72 times, starting from [-20, 20]'. Sections 14.1 and 14.15 say the numpy code is 'the shooting method of the Revision Rust solver' including 'bisection on the labels'. Line 2216 says 'The two programs do the same arithmetic'. The Rust solver actually uses a different method: it expands a bracket from a guess and then iterates a safeguarded Newton step (using dPhi/deps) with bisection fallback, down to a tolerance. Only the RK4 integration and the Pruefer angle are the same.
findings.evidence: Revision/kohn_sham/solver/src/shoot.rs: find_level(ctx, sec, t, guess, lower, tol), lines 201-308. Bracket expansion uses 'step *= 2.0'; the iteration uses 'let mut en = ec - gc / dc; let bisect = !(en > lo && en < hi) || gc.abs() > 0.5 * prev_abs;' and stops at 'hi - lo <= tol'. There is no fixed 72-step bisection of [-20, 20]; that loop is only in the notebooks ('iterations=72', 'np.full(k.shape, -20.0)').
findings.fix: State that the notebooks use plain bisection (72 halvings of [-20, 20]) on the same Phi, while the Rust solver uses a safeguarded Newton-bisection to a tolerance. Both find the root of the same discretised Phi, which is why they agree to 1e-11. Change 'do the same arithmetic' to 'integrate the same RK4 discretisation'.

findings.location: Section 14.26, 'Why every symmetric occupation has rho = (nB + SC)/16' (lines 3467-3511)
findings.problem: Two problems. First, the conclusion drops a hypothesis. The derivation fills all eight positive-energy modes of a momentum equally ('these eight modes, all filled, contribute G_p B'), but the result is stated 'for every occupation that is symmetric under p -> -p'. A p/-p-symmetric occupation of only some of the eight degenerate modes does not, in general, give a combination of B and C. The record keeps the hypothesis ('the 8-fold good-sector gas'). Second, the mixed products of different gammas are dismissed with 'in the same way ... cancel in pairs', the 'similarly' that the deep-dive rule forbids.

Line 3467: 'and in the same way the products of $\gamma^{(x_4)}\gamma^{(a)}$ and $\gamma^{(x_4)}\gamma^{(b)}$ for $a \ne b$ cancel in pairs'.
findings.fix: State the hypothesis: the eight degenerate modes of each momentum carry the same occupation, as in closed shells and Mermin states, and p and -p are equally occupied. Write out the line (g4 ga)(g4 gb) + (g4 gb)(g4 ga) = ga gb + gb ga = 0 for a != b.

findings.problem: Deep-dive gap. The text asserts without reason that 'The average over directions is the same as the projection onto the matrices that commute with the rotations of 3-space'. A closed lattice shell is a finite cubic set of directions, not all of SO(3). The equality holds because End(16) carries only spin 0 and spin 1, so the cubic average equals the full rotation average, which in turn is the projection onto the commutant. That reason is in the record but missing from the chapter, so the step is unsupported for the student.
findings.evidence: ks-theory-python.json, exchange_slab_exact_fock detail: '(= the projection onto the 64-dim commutant of the 3-space rotations; End(16) carries only spin 0 and 1)'. ks-theory-wolfram.json: 'averaged over the 48-element spinor octahedral group (End(16) carries spin 0 and 1 only, so this equals the full SO(3) average)'.
findings.fix: Add the two missing sentences: averaging over a group projects onto the matrices invariant under it, and for matrices that carry only spin 0 and spin 1 the cubic (octahedral) average already equals the full rotation average (record, both reports).
